assets.name: Bottle
assets.description: The bar's all-purpose bottle: lines the back-bar shelves, sits on every table, and is the main improvised weapon in the bar fight (grab, throw, or smash over someone).
notes: Origin at the base centre, Y up.
Six glass colours and three label colours are mixed along the shelves; a variant set (or a tintable material) keeps that variety.
When thrown it spins end over end, so the silhouette should read from any angle.
Held in the first-person fight anchor and in patrons' right hands.

assets.name: Pint glass (half-finished)
assets.description: A pint of lager left on the bar and tables, and the glass the regulars hold while they drink.
notes: Origin at the base centre; Y up. The base sits exactly on the surface it is placed on.
Keep the liquid as its own mesh, anchored at the base: drinking scales its height down from the bottom (setGlassLevel), and the foam layer rides on top of it.
The glass shell is drawn transparent after the liquid (renderOrder 2 vs 1); keep the shell thin and open-topped so the liquid reads through it.

assets.name: Rocks glass
assets.description: Short glass with a spirit in it. Sits on the tables and is a throwable in the bar fight (lighter than a bottle).
notes: Origin at the base centre; Y up. The base sits exactly on the surface it is placed on.
Keep the liquid as its own mesh, anchored at the base: drinking scales its height down from the bottom (setGlassLevel), and the foam layer rides on top of it.
The glass shell is drawn transparent after the liquid (renderOrder 2 vs 1); keep the shell thin and open-topped so the liquid reads through it.

assets.name: Pool cue
assets.description: Two-piece cue: ash shaft with a blue tip and a dark wrapped butt. Used by you (first person and on the table) and by Shark.
usedIn: Billiards: your cue on the table
notes: Origin at the tip, the stick runs along -Z. The aim, power pull-back and strike all move it along that axis.
Current length is 1.88 m (longer than a real 1.47 m cue); a regulation cue is fine, the code places it by the tip.

assets.name: Pool balls (full set)
assets.description: Sixteen balls: cue ball, solids 1 to 7, the 8, and stripes 9 to 15, shown racked. Each ball's texture is generated (number circle on both sides; stripes are a band).
usedIn: A few sit on the pool table between games (plain colours)
notes: Radius must stay 28.6 mm (57.2 mm diameter): the physics simulation uses it.
Balls roll by rotating the mesh, so put the numbers and stripes in a texture (or UV layout) that reads while rolling.

assets.name: Dart
assets.description: Steel-tip dart: needle point, knurled tungsten barrel, nylon shaft with a gold ring, four printed flights. Blue flights are yours, red are Fergus's (shown side by side).
usedIn: Darts thrown by regulars at the board
notes: Origin at the point, the dart points along +Z. It is aimed by pointing +Z along its flight path and spins about that axis, and sticks into the board 8 mm deep.
About 139 mm long; flights span 35 mm.
Flights are self-lit slightly so they read with the board light in front of them; a flight texture with team colour is enough.

notes: Hangs from the rack hook at 1.7 m.

assets.name: Your coat

usedIn: Opening: carried in first person and hung on the rack

assets.name: Pool table
assets.description: Seven-foot bar table: dark wood frame, green felt bed and cushions, six pockets, four square legs.
notes: Physics constraint: the playing surface (inside the cushions) is 2.30 x 1.15 m and the bed top sits at 0.82 m. Pockets are at the four corners and the middle of each long side (corner mouths 68 mm, side 58 mm). Keep these or update poolPhysics.js.
Origin at floor level under the table centre; the long axis runs along X.
The camera gets very close to the felt and the rails when aiming, so they deserve the most texture detail.

assets.name: Cue rack
assets.description: Four house cues standing against the wall behind the pool table.
usedIn: East wall by the pool table
notes: Decorative only; a proper wall rack holding these would improve it.
assets.pivot: placed in world space (no local origin); bottom centre recommended

assets.name: Dartboard and cabinet
assets.description: Regulation bristle board (451 mm) with a printed number ring, in a dark wood cabinet panel.
notes: Scoring constraint: the board face is a disc of radius 225.5 mm; the double ring's outer edge is at 80% of it (180 mm) and all other rings scale from there (treble 58 to 63%, outer bull 9.4%, bull 3.7% of 180 mm). 20 at the top, numbers clockwise 20, 1, 18, 4, 13, 6, 10, 15, 2, 17, 3, 19, 7, 16, 8, 11, 14, 9, 12, 5. Keep the layout exact or scoring stops matching what players see.
Board centre is 1.73 m off the floor; the face points into the room.
During darts the board fills most of the screen, so it needs a high-resolution face texture (the current one is 2048 px).
assets.pivot: placed in world space (no local origin); bottom centre recommended

assets.name: Foosball table
assets.description: Wooden foosball table with a printed pitch, open box sides, two goals, metal legs and eight rods. The bar version shown here uses simple block figures; the playable figures are the next entry.
notes: Physics constraint: the pitch is 1.20 x 0.70 m with its surface at 0.77 m; goals are 0.20 m wide in the middle of each end; rod rows are 0.15 m apart at x = -0.525 to +0.525. Keep these or update foosball.js.
Origin at floor level under the table centre; long axis along X.
During foosball the camera looks down the length of the table from behind your goal, filling the screen, so the pitch and inner walls need the most detail.

assets.name: Foosball rod (3 figures)
assets.description: A playable rod: steel bar, rubber handle on its owner's side, figures fixed to it. Rods come with 3 (goalie, forwards, defence on one side), 2 or 5 figures.
notes: Origin on the rod axis at the table's centre line; Z runs across the table. The rod slides along Z and spins about Z.
The selected rod's handle is recoloured amber; keep the handle a separate mesh or material.

assets.name: Foosball figure
assets.description: One figure on a rod, in your blue and Nadia's red (shown side by side).
notes: Origin where the rod passes through the chest; the feet hang 7 cm below it. Kick physics uses that foot length (65 mm from the rod axis).
Spins full circles on the rod, so it must look right upside down.
Two team colours: blue (you) and red (opponent).

assets.name: Fight arms and boot
assets.description: Your arms in the bar fight: two arms (sleeve to fist) for punching and blocking, and a boot that swings up for kicks. A grabbed bottle or glass is held at an anchor in front of the right hand.
notes: Camera-local: the camera is at the origin looking down -Z, 72 degree field of view. Each arm hangs from a shoulder pivot (x = +/-0.30, y = -0.32) and bends at an elbow pivot.
Guard, punch, high block and low block poses rotate those two pivots; keep them as separate bones.
The boot is normally hidden and only shown during a kick.

assets.name: Drinking hand
assets.description: Your right hand and sleeve in the drinking contest. Reaches down to the bar, takes the glass, brings it to your mouth and tips it back.
notes: Camera-local; origin at the palm centre. The glass is parented to the hand while drinking, sitting 3 cm below the palm.
Rotates about X up to about 65 degrees to tip the glass toward the mouth.

assets.name: Cue in hand and chalk
assets.description: While it is not your shot: your cue held low in the right hand, tip up and away. The left hand holds a cube of blue chalk and rubs the tip when you chalk your cue.
notes: Camera-local. The chalking animation swings the cue tip up in front of the camera and moves the chalk hand to it.
The chalk hand is shown here beside the cue; in game it only appears while chalking.
